name: FreeToken
description: FreeToken brings datacenter-scale model serving to your desktop. Run massive models locally, fast and efficiently.
readmeExcerpt:
| Download | Paper | Developer Slack | Community Discord | Community WeChat |

Unlock datacenter-class intelligence on the hardware you already own — Run 290B+ frontier MoE models locally on your gaming PC at blistering interactive speeds. ## About FreeToken is an edge-native Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) serving engine designed for running frontier-scale open-weight models on personal and consumer hardware. It treats heterogeneous edge resources—GPUs, CPUs, host memory, and interconnects—as a unified, elastic inference platform. Its core features include: - **Fast Edge-Native Runtime**: Provides efficient MoE serving with bandwidth-adaptive CPU–GPU co-execution ($q^\star$ policy), full-layer double-buffered prefill streaming, global LRU expert caching, graph-compatible execution, and the FTW fast weight format. - **Semantic-Aware Caching**: Features semantic anchor checkpoints for recurrent state and KV caches, allowing agentic context edits (e.g., tool calls, thinking blocks) to avoid redundant context recomputation. - **Elastic Memory Management**: Supports dynamic, runtime VRAM re-allocation between expert caches and KV memory without engine restarts or weight reloading. - **Broad MoE & Ecosystem Support**: Supports frontier open-weight MoE models (e.g., DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, GLM-5.2) across various parameter scales and quantization formats (e.g., MXFP4, NVFP4, FP8, BF16, GGUF), with Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible APIs for seamless integration with real-world coding and tool-calling agents (e.g., Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenClaw, DeepSeek Harness). - **Diverse Consumer Hardware**: Scales across consumer laptops, gaming desktops, and workstation GPUs, with native support for NVIDIA RTX 30, RTX 40, and RTX 50 series GPUs. ## Getting Started ### Desktop app Download FreeToken for Windows or Linux at [flashml.ai](https://www.flashml.ai/). It sets the engine up for you and gives you a GUI for running models, chatting, and tuning the engine.
### CLI Install FreeToken with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) (recommended) or pip: ```bash uv pip install "freetoken[accel]" ``` Or build from source: ```bash git clone https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken.git && cd FreeToken uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install -e ".[accel]" ``` For More details: - [Install FreeToken](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/install.md) - [Quick start](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md) - [Supported models](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/models.md) - [CLI reference](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/cli.md) - [Repairing old FTW checkpoints](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/ftw-hotfix.md) - [Diagnosing a checkpoint that fails to load](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/scripts/checkpoint_diagnose/README.md) ## Citation If you use FreeToken for your research, please cite our [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16157): ```bibtex @article{yang2026freetoken, title={FreeToken: Efficient Edge-Native MoE Serving with Bandwidth-Adaptive Execution}, author={Yang, Shuo and Fan, Xiaoze and Pan, Melissa and Xi, Haocheng and Wang, Zhe and Sun, Shanlin and Keutzer, Kurt and Han, Song and Zaharia, Matei and Xu, Chenfeng and Stoica, Ion}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.16157}, year={2026} } ``` ## Acknowledgment FreeToken was deeply inspired by [mini-sglang](https://github.com/sgl-project/mini-sglang), and learned the design and reused code from the following projects: [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang), [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm), [FlashInfer](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer), [flash-linear-attention](https://github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention), [LightLLM](https://github.com/ModelTC/lightllm) and [llama.cpp](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp). ## License [Apache License 2.0](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/LICENSE).

releases.body:
## FreeToken nightly (rolling)

Automated build of `main`. This release is **overwritten every night**: the `nightly` tag moves to the built commit and the previous wheels are deleted. Do not pin to this tag; pin to a wheel URL below, whose filename embeds the commit it was built from.

**Install** (Linux x86_64, CPython 3.12, CUDA 13.0):

```bash
uv pip install \
  "freetoken[accel] @ https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/releases/download/nightly/freetoken-0.2.2%2Bg66190a937-cp312-cp312-linux_x86_64.whl" \
  "https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/releases/download/nightly/freetoken_kernel_cache-0.2.2%2Bcu130.g66190a937-py3-none-linux_x86_64.whl"
```

releases.body:
## Highlights

- **Speculative decoding.** `--speculative-algorithm mtp` drafts with the checkpoint's own MTP layer, and `--speculative-algorithm dflash` drafts with a separate DFlash 2 checkpoint (#836, #844, #856, #857).
- **New model.** Ripple-65B Preview, from BF16 safetensors, the ModelOpt NVFP4 export or GGUF (#871).
- **Faster CPU experts in `hybrid`.** The NVFP4 W4A8 CPU kernels are faster; rerun `ft bench bw` so `hybrid` uses the new CPU rate (#851).

## Speculative Decoding

Each decode step drafts k tokens and verifies them on the target in one forward, so one step can commit several tokens. With sampling, the output distribution stays the target's. Speculative decoding is off by default, and the draft stays on the GPU, so it takes some KV and expert cache space. See the [flags](https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken/blob/main/docs/cli.md#speculative-decoding).

releases.name: v0.2.1
releases.body:
## Highlights

- [Feature] **Image input for GGUF models.** A llama.cpp mmproj file next to the model, or one passed with `--mmproj`, adds image input to Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.8, Gemma-4, GLM-5.3-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp GGUF files (#803, #810, #816).
- [Feature] **More GGUF archs.** `deepseek4` (DeepSeek-V4 Flash, Flash-0731, Pro, Pro-0813) (#774), `qwen3vl` and `qwen3vlmoe` (text only) (#807).
- [Feature] **Support Flint**, from BF16 safetensors, the ModelOpt NVFP4 export or the official NVFP4 GGUF (#797).
- [Feature] **Embedding table in host RAM.** `--embed-weights host` keeps the input token embedding table in pinned host RAM and gives its VRAM to the expert cache and KV: decode is 8.7% faster on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with 24 GiB of free VRAM (#806).

## GGUF Support

- [Feature] **Image input from an mmproj file** (#803). llama.cpp keeps the vision tower in a separate `mmproj-*.gguf`. Without `--mmproj`, FreeToken takes a `*mmproj*.gguf` that fits the model (output width, tower type, image tokens) from the model file's own folder, BF16 before F32, F16 and quantized files; the log names the file it loads. releases.body:
## Highlights

- **GGUF Support.** llama.cpp GGUF files serve directly with `ft serve --model <local file>.gguf`; quantized tensors run on llama.cpp's own kernels (ggml-cuda on the GPU, ggml-cpu for `hybrid` / `cpu` experts). Supported GGUF archs:
  - `qwen2` (Qwen2 / Qwen2.5), `qwen3` and `qwen3moe` (Qwen3 dense and MoE)
  - `qwen35` and `qwen35moe` (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 dense and MoE, Qwen3.8-27B), `qwen4exp` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next)
  - `gemma4` (Gemma-4 12B, 26B-A4B, 31B)
  - `llama` (Llama 3.x, and Mistral files converted before llama.cpp's `mistral3` arch)
  - `muse-glimmer` (Muse-Glimmer)
  - `minimax-m2` (MiniMax-M2 / M2.x), `minimax-m3` (MiniMax-M3)
  - `glm4moe` (GLM-4.5, GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.6, GLM-4.7), `glm5-next` (GLM-5.3-Flash)
- **Support new models.**
  - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, text and images (#603)

releases.name: v0.1.3
releases.body:
## Highlights

- **Image input.** Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.6, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Gemma-4, GLM-5.3-Flash, MiniMax-M3 and Muse-Glimmer-30B accept images through the OpenAI, Anthropic and Responses APIs. Vision towers stream their weights from host memory; `--text-model-only` serves a multimodal checkpoint as text.
- **Support new models.** 
  - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (#257) 
  - GLM-5.3-Flash (#332).
- **Quantization rebuilt** (#418). One `QuantConfig` → `QuantScheme` → kernel path for every layer; kernels are selected with `--quant-backend layer[.kind]=name`, and `--moe-backend` becomes `--moe-strategy`.

## Multimodal

FreeToken now serves vision-language models (#454): an image goes through the checkpoint's own processor and vision tower, then down the same scheduler, radix cache and MoE offload path as text.

- **Engine**: image spans are content-keyed in the radix cache; encoded embeddings sit in an encoder cache between prefill chunks; the vision tower streams its weights from pinned host memory two blocks at a time.

| Download | Paper | Developer Slack | Community Discord | Community WeChat |

Unlock datacenter-class intelligence on the hardware you already own — Run 290B+ frontier MoE models locally on your gaming PC at blistering interactive speeds.

About

FreeToken is an edge-native Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) serving engine designed for running frontier-scale open-weight models on personal and consumer hardware. It treats heterogeneous edge resources—GPUs, CPUs, host memory, and interconnects—as a unified, elastic inference platform. Its core features include:

  • Fast Edge-Native Runtime: Provides efficient MoE serving with bandwidth-adaptive CPU–GPU co-execution ($q^\star$ policy), full-layer double-buffered prefill streaming, global LRU expert caching, graph-compatible execution, and the FTW fast weight format.
  • Semantic-Aware Caching: Features semantic anchor checkpoints for recurrent state and KV caches, allowing agentic context edits (e.g., tool calls, thinking blocks) to avoid redundant context recomputation.
  • Elastic Memory Management: Supports dynamic, runtime VRAM re-allocation between expert caches and KV memory without engine restarts or weight reloading.
  • Broad MoE & Ecosystem Support: Supports frontier open-weight MoE models (e.g., DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, GLM-5.2) across various parameter scales and quantization formats (e.g., MXFP4, NVFP4, FP8, BF16, GGUF), with Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible APIs for seamless integration with real-world coding and tool-calling agents (e.g., Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenClaw, DeepSeek Harness).
  • Diverse Consumer Hardware: Scales across consumer laptops, gaming desktops, and workstation GPUs, with native support for NVIDIA RTX 30, RTX 40, and RTX 50 series GPUs.

Getting Started

Desktop app

Download FreeToken for Windows or Linux at flashml.ai. It sets the engine up for you and gives you a GUI for running models, chatting, and tuning the engine.

CLI

Install FreeToken with uv (recommended) or pip:

uv pip install "freetoken[accel]"

Or build from source:

git clone https://github.com/FlashML-org/FreeToken.git && cd FreeToken
uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[accel]"

For More details:

  • Install FreeToken
  • Quick start
  • Supported models
  • CLI reference
  • Repairing old FTW checkpoints
  • Diagnosing a checkpoint that fails to load

Citation

If you use FreeToken for your research, please cite our paper:

@article{yang2026freetoken,
  title={FreeToken: Efficient Edge-Native MoE Serving with Bandwidth-Adaptive Execution},
  author={Yang, Shuo and Fan, Xiaoze and Pan, Melissa and Xi, Haocheng and Wang, Zhe and Sun, Shanlin and Keutzer, Kurt and Han, Song and Zaharia, Matei and Xu, Chenfeng and Stoica, Ion},
  journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2608.16157},
  year={2026}
}

Acknowledgment

FreeToken was deeply inspired by mini-sglang, and learned the design and reused code from the following projects: SGLang, vLLM, FlashInfer, flash-linear-attention, LightLLM and llama.cpp.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An edge-native MoE serving engine for running frontier-scale AI models on personal hardware.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: FreeToken is a high-performance inference engine optimized for running massive Mixture-of-Experts models locally on consumer hardware. It treats heterogeneous edge resources like GPUs, CPUs, and system memory as a unified compute platform to handle models scaling up to 290 billion parameters. The engine utilizes advanced memory management, semantic caching, and bandwidth-adaptive co-execution to deliver blistering interactive speeds. It provides OpenAI-compatible APIs, allowing seamless integration with existing tools and frameworks.
keyFeatures: CPU-GPU co-execution: Adapts to hardware bandwidth to efficiently split inference tasks across available processors.
Semantic-aware caching: Avoids redundant recomputation by anchoring recurrent state and KV caches during agentic workflows.
Dynamic memory management: Re-allocates VRAM between expert caches and KV memory at runtime without restarting the engine.
Frontier MoE support: Runs massive open-weight models like DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Qwen3.6 across various quantization formats.
Standardized API: Exposes an Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible endpoint for easy drop-in replacement in existing apps.

useCases.title: Local AI assistance
useCases.description: Run powerful LLMs entirely on a personal gaming PC for private, offline coding assistance.

useCases.title: Agentic workflow acceleration
useCases.description: Execute multi-step AI agent tasks efficiently using semantic caching to minimize context reprocessing.

useCases.title: Cost-free inference
useCases.description: Deploy high-quality MoE models locally to avoid the API costs associated with cloud-hosted frontier models.

useCases.title: Edge deployment
useCases.description: Serve capable AI models in environments with restricted internet access or strict data privacy requirements.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: AI enthusiasts, researchers, and developers with consumer GPU hardware. It is designed for users wanting to run massive MoE models without enterprise server equipment.
